changeset-claim-re-read

## ⚠️ 2 pending changeset(s) describe a file this change touches

Their bodies publish **verbatim** into the CHANGELOG at the next release, so this is a request to **re-read them against your diff** — addressed here because you are the one seat that can answer it without re-deriving anything.

⛔ Nothing here blocks, and nothing here is a verdict on your change. This gate exits 0, is not a required context, and judges **name resolution, never meaning**: it asked whether a pending body names a file you touched. "Is this sentence still true?" is the one question it will not answer, and the one you are being asked to answer.

### `.changeset/9786-detail-timestamps-display-locale.md`

- names `machineLocaleCensus-9909.test.ts` → `packages/i18n/src/__tests__/machineLocaleCensus-9909.test.ts` — edited by this change

  > **Two instruments land with the repair, because the repair alone is what happened the last five times.** `detailTimestamps.displayLocale-9786.test.tsx` renders every surface whose face reaches the DOM under a declared `de-DE` session and a declared `en` one and requires the two readings to differ — an assertion the runner's own locale cannot satisfy, since before this change both legs came from the machine and were byte-identical whatever the machine was. It also patches the `Intl` constructors and `Date.prototype.toLocale*` and inspects the argument each call actually receives, which is the only way to catch a variable that resolves to `undefined`, and the only way to reach `RecordMetaFooter` — whose absolute face is a `TooltipContent` child that Radix keeps out of the DOM until the tooltip opens. A census pin reddens when a new bare, `undefined`- or hard-coded-tag call site is written; it masks comments before it counts, and it declares `InlineFieldInput`'s `en-CA` as an exemption with its reason — that call feeds `ANGLE-BRACKETS(input type="date")`, whose value HTML defines as `YYYY-MM-DD`, so it is an ISO formatter and not a display locale. It landed scoped to this package and, under the ruling on this card, became the one repository-wide census in `@object-ui/i18n` (`machineLocaleCensus-9909.test.ts`, objectui#9909), which carries that exemption forward.

### `.changeset/9909-machine-locale-sweep.md`

- names `machineLocaleCensus-9909.test.ts` → `packages/i18n/src/__tests__/machineLocaleCensus-9909.test.ts` — edited by this change

  > **One census, repository-wide.** `plugin-detail`'s machine-locale census pin (objectui#9786) is now a single test, `machineLocaleCensus-9909.test.ts` in `@object-ui/i18n`, covering every workspace package whose manifest depends on `@object-ui/i18n`. It refuses any call site that passes nothing, `undefined`, the `'default'` pseudo-tag (a subtag no locale data answers, so `Intl` resolves it to the machine's locale) or a hard-coded tag, unless the site is declared with its reason — for example the `catch` fallback for a tag `Intl` itself rejected, or an ISO formatter feeding `ANGLE-BRACKETS(input type="date")`. Each declared site is counted exactly, so deleting one without its entry is refused too. The per-package pin it replaces is deleted. The runtime tripwire that observes the argument each locale-taking call (`Intl` constructors, `Date` and `Number` `toLocale*`) actually receives moved into the private `@object-ui/test-support` package, and every surface above is pinned with it: the same data under two declared locales must render differently, NO locale-taking call may receive the machine's locale (nothing, `undefined` or `'default'`), and the surface's own calls must receive the declared tag. A call carrying another declared tag, such as the `'en'` of the session's UI language, is tolerated by design: only the machine's locale is the defect.

Read the **paragraph**, not the line: both false halves of the objectui#8617 claim sat in one paragraph, and correcting either alone would have left it asserting the same wrong thing.

If a claim did go false, **correct the body**. That is precedented and prose-only, frontmatter untouched; `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs` will report the correction as its own case 2 ("correcting a declaration on purpose … legitimate"), which is the intended shape — one gate asks for the read, the other records the write.

Not covered, stated so nobody reads this as more: a born-false claim that spells no line address at all (objectui#9495 coordinated one by ORDINAL — "a grep finds that member first" — and deciding that means reading what the sentence means), a claim spelled as a symbol or a package rather than a backticked file name, and a file named ambiguously.

Angle-bracketed names in the quoted prose above are rewritten as `ANGLE-BRACKETS(name)`: GitHub deletes tag-shaped fragments from a stored body, and a quote that silently loses the identifier it is about is worse than a visible repair.

Compared the checked-out tree with `3335767b4` (merge-base with origin/main): 6 file(s) changed outside `.changeset/`, read against 1371 pending declaration(s) that publish a body (1946 pending in total). · [run](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectui/actions/runs/36079452622)

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `5a40f03e0d6e92a338335bf00ffc291ea55e7099`

Rendered by an isolated review subagent spawned by the `domain:ui#4` seat; its served tier was checked against its transcript stamps (95 of 95 model stamps at the review tier). Adopted by this seat.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Identity.** `GET pulls/10431` resolves `head.sha` to `5a40f03e0d6e92a338335bf00ffc291ea55e7099`, the expected value. One commit, whose parent is `74fcda8292280167a4c22f6edf6586f29135b7da`, which is also the merge-base with `origin/main`: the dev's stated base `74fcda829` is the real one. Read the card body, the triage comment `5823975048`, the claim `5824390875` and the dev report `5824824057` before the code.
- **(a) Completeness: 2 at base, 0 at head, confirmed twice.** A `git grep` over the whole non-test tree at head for `toLocaleDateString`, `toLocaleString`, `toLocaleTimeString` and `Intl.*Format` whose first argument is `language` or `*.language` returns no source hit. The only residual matches are prose: `CHANGELOG.md` and `ROADMAP.md` quoting a past `data-table` change, and a JSON string in `skills/objectui/evals/i18n.json` that spells `navigator.language`; none is code. The same grep at `74fcda829` and at today's `origin/main` (`9ec8ceba06`) finds exactly two source hits, `ApprovalsInboxPage.tsx` (`formatRelative`'s catch line) and `CommentThread.tsx` (`formatAbsoluteDate`'s try), the card's two sites. A multi-line-aware scan of the head tree (first argument on its own line) and a variant grep for `i18n.language`, `resolvedLanguage` and `language ||` / `language ??` fallbacks also return 0. A census-shaped probe (same manifest-derived population of 22 packages, same tooling filter, same comment masker, same matcher) counts 2 `language`-named first arguments at base, both the card's sites, and 0 at head. The dev's measurement holds.
- **(a) Adjacent sites the class also covers, outside the strict target and outside this card.** A supplementary grep for helpers handed the UI language as a `locale` option finds four places where a date face still formats with the translation hook's `language` rather than `useDisplayLocale()`; none is a direct `toLocale*` / `Intl` first argument named `language`, so neither the census nor the proposed name rule sees them, and none is in this card's scope (the card and triage grade exactly two sites): `packages/components/src/renderers/complex/data-table.tsx` (`formatDateTime(value, { locale: language })` and `formatDate(value, undefined, { locale: language })`, `language` from `useTableTranslation()`; core's `DateDisplayOptions.locale` is documented as the BCP-47 display locale); `packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordDetailView.tsx` (audit history `fmtCtx = { t, locale: language, lookupLabels }`, which `formatScalar` in `auditHistoryDisplay.ts` spends on `toLocaleDateString` / `toLocaleString`); `packages/plugin-gantt/src/ResourceWorkload.tsx` (`const locale = language || undefined`, then `toLocaleDateString(locale, …)`, with a machine-locale fallthrough on an empty language); `packages/plugin-calendar/src/CalendarView.tsx` (`effectiveLocale = locale !== "default" ? locale : language`, where the `locale` prop defaults to `"default"`). The other `locale: language` hits (`RecordDetailView` action params, `useConsoleActionRuntime`, `FlowRunner`, `usePackageL10n`) resolve per-locale label maps, a translation choice, not a formatter. Facts for the seat; not defects of this PR.
- **(b) Fidelity to the objectui#10331 shape: matches PR objectui#10369's diff.** Both sites call `useDisplayLocale()` in the component body with no `??` / `||` fallback (`const displayLocale = useDisplayLocale();`), the same line the sibling wrote in `InstalledList` and `CloudConnectionPanel`. `ApprovalsInboxPage` reuses the page's pre-existing `displayLocale` (already read for `formatDate`, `decisionAmountEntry` and `payloadSummary`); the diff changes only the destructure (`language` dropped), the `formatRelative` date line and its dependency list (`[tr, displayLocale, now]`). `CommentThread` threads `displayLocale` through `formatTimestamp(iso, t, locale)` into `formatAbsoluteDate(date, locale)`, parameter renamed `locale` at both signatures and both call sites; the inner `try { toLocaleDateString(locale) } catch { toLocaleDateString() }` is byte-identical apart from the rename. `language` is no longer destructured in either file and every remaining mention is in a comment. Both doc comments are rewritten and read true against the hook: the display locale is `locale || language || 'en'`, so a session with no regional locale renders exactly as under objectui#3441, and with no provider the hook answers the same tag the translation hook did. `@object-ui/collaboration` already depends on `@object-ui/i18n` (`workspace:*`), which exports `useDisplayLocale` from its index; no dependency added.
- **(c) No-provider behaviour (A1) verified from source.** `useDisplayLocale()` returns `locale || language || 'en'` where `useLocalization()` reads a context created with `{}` (so `locale` is `undefined` with no provider) and `useObjectTranslation().language` is `context?.language || i18n.language || 'en'`; with no instance `i18n` is an empty object, so the answer is the string `'en'`, never `undefined`. `useCollaborationTranslation` is a `createSafeTranslation` hook that returns `language: result.language` from that same `useObjectTranslation()`, so the tag is identical to what the branch passed before. The added case in `comment-thread-no-provider-fallback.test.tsx` spies on `Date.prototype.toLocaleDateString` and asserts every recorded call equals `['en']`, which is exactly that claim. `it(` count is 15 at base and 16 at head; the diff touches only the vitest import (adds `vi`), `afterEach` (adds `vi.restoreAllMocks()`), one docblock and the new case; no existing case body changed, and the file still imports nothing from `@object-ui/i18n`.
- **(d) The census control is still lit.** The only change to `machineLocaleCensus-9909.test.ts` is the `reason` string of the `CommentThread.tsx` DECLARED entry; `file`, `expression` (`return date.toLocaleDateString();`) and `count: 1` are unchanged. At head the raw file contains that expression exactly once as code (the catch of `formatAbsoluteDate`); the second textual occurrence is inside `formatTimestamp`'s doc comment, which the census masks, and the census-shaped probe reports exactly one bare site in that file. The new reason text ("whose `try` already passes the display locale (`useDisplayLocale()`, objectui#10375; the session language before that)") is true at head. The lit-control assertion (`control.map(text)` equals `['return date.toLocaleDateString();']` and is declared) holds; the width guards hold too (22 packages, 1273 sources, 127 sites).
- **(e) The pins are real and can fail.** Both new files mount the real `I18nProvider` (`defaultLanguage: 'en'`, `detectBrowserLanguage: false`, `persistLanguage={false}`) and the real `LocalizationProvider` (`value={{ locale }}`), both exported from `@object-ui/i18n`, the same harness as the objectui#10331 pins. `comment-thread-display-locale-10375.test.tsx` (6 cases): de-CH pin `4.3.2020` also asserted equal to the runtime's own `de-CH` rendering, en-US control `3/4/2020`, the differential (de-CH reading not equal to en-US reading), an argument spy asserting every `toLocaleDateString` call received `de-CH`, the three-day-old relative-bucket control (`3d ago` under de-CH), and the malformed `de_CH` case (runtime date, never the raw ISO). `ApprovalsInboxPage.displayLocale-10375.test.tsx` (5 cases): the same pin, control, differential and relative-bucket control, read from the queue cell whose `title` is the untouched `formatDate` face, plus the `@object-ui/test-support` tripwire (`recordLocaleArgumentsAsync`, `isMachineLocale`, which flags `argc === 0`, `undefined` or `'default'`). Its `vi.mock`s double only auth, the adapter and the approvals API, not the locale channel. The console pin has no malformed-tag case; the dev says why (that catch returns the raw ISO string, flagged as out of scope rather than pinned). Ablation arithmetic: 6 + 5 + 16 = 27 cases per leg. CommentThread leg red = de-CH pin, differential, argument spy = 3, green 24; ApprovalsInbox leg red = de-CH pin, differential, tripwire = 3, green 24. Consistent with the case lists, and the reported red readings (`3/4/2020` where `4.3.2020` was expected; `saw: [["en"]]`) are what a `language`-fed formatter produces under an English UI.
- **(f) Changeset truth.** `.changeset/10375-comment-and-inbox-dates-display-locale.md` declares `@object-ui/collaboration: patch` and `@object-ui/console: patch`. Every sentence checks out at head: the seven-or-more-days branch of `formatTimestamp` (a `days` count below 7 returns the bucket, else `formatAbsoluteDate`) now takes `useDisplayLocale()`; it used to take the UI language; the `3/4/2020` to `4.3.2020` reading is the pin; the no-display-locale and no-provider fallthrough is the hook's `locale || language || 'en'`; the malformed-locale fallback is the kept inner catch; `formatRelative` shows a date once `Math.round(hr / 24)` reaches 30, called on `submitted_at`, `completed_at` and the history rows' `created_at`; the relative words stay on `t` / `tr`. One precision note, not a falsehood: the day count is a nested rounding (seconds, then minutes, then hours, then days), so "rounded to the nearest day" is a simplification at the 30-day edge.
